name: Derevi, Empyrial Tactician + Gaea's Cradle -> bonus Cradle activation from a connecting attacker

prerequisites.timing: Combat damage step - Derevi's ability triggers 'whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player'.
targets_required: Derevi's triggered ability targets a permanent to tap or untap - target Gaea's Cradle.
other: NOT a loop and NOT infinite by itself - checked against Commander Spellbook (query for card="Derevi, Empyrial Tactician" card="Gaea's Cradle" together) which returns exactly one variant, 2404-2608-4499, and it additionally requires Emiel the Blessed (not in this exact 98-card list; Emiel already appears in interactions/one_card_away_from_deck.json as a recurring high-popularity missing piece across multiple lines). Without Emiel, this is a one-shot value trigger per attacker, not a loop.

Derevi's oracle text: 'Flying / When Derevi enters and whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, you may tap or untap target permanent.' - a normal (non-doubled) triggered ability, one instance per creature dealing combat damage.

SCOPE NOTE on the original candidate writeup's 'scales with attacker count' claim: only the single-attacker base case (one Derevi trigger, one untap-then-retap of Gaea's Cradle) was engine-verified below. A two-attacker extension (two simultaneous trigger instances, each independently untapping-then-retapping Cradle in turn) was attempted but not completed within this session's engine-reproduction effort - the underlying rules mechanism supports the scaling claim being plausible (CR 603.2c: an ability triggers once per occurrence of its trigger event, so N connecting creatures produce N independent trigger instances; CR 603.3b: the controller orders those simultaneously-pending triggers before any of them resolve; CR 117.3b: the active player receives priority after each individual ability resolves, before the next object on the stack resolves - this is the specific mechanism that would let Cradle be tapped again between the first trigger's resolution and the second trigger's resolution), but it is downgraded from 'verified' to 'plausible, not itself engine-tested' until a dedicated test succeeds. Tracked as a residual gap (coverage_backlog SIM-0012), not asserted as fact.

CR 500.5 / 106.4 (mana pool empties at the end of each step/phase) means any mana produced by tapping Gaea's Cradle before combat does NOT carry into the combat damage step - what persists across steps is the permanent's TAPPED status, not stored mana. This is why Derevi's untap effect is what enables a second Cradle activation that turn, not merely delayed use of the same mana.

result.summary: One additional Gaea's Cradle activation (untap a previously-tapped Cradle, then tap it again for mana within the same combat damage step) from a single connecting attacker - a real, bounded (not infinite) mana bump. Whether this scales linearly with additional connecting attackers in the same combat is plausible per the underlying rules mechanism but not itself engine-verified (see scope note).

rules_citations: CR 500.5 / 106.4 — a player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase; this is why the pre-combat tap's mana doesn't persist into the combat damage step, isolating the interaction to Gaea's Cradle's tapped/untapped status (a permanent characteristic, not mana pool content).

CR 603.2c — an ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs, but can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences; each creature dealing combat damage to a player is counted separately.
CR 603.3b — a player puts each of their own simultaneously-pending triggered abilities on the stack in any order they choose.

CR 117.3b — the active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves. This is the specific mechanism (not 603.3b, which only governs the order abilities are PUT on the stack) that would let Gaea's Cradle be tapped again between one trigger's resolution and the next's, per the scope note above.

executable_engine_check.notes: Reproduces this record's own stated transition end-to-end, scoped exactly to the single-attacker base case (per result.summary) - not the un-engine-tested multi-attacker extension (see the scope note in prerequisites.other and coverage_backlog SIM-0012). Reproduced in the same from-source Maven build of magefree/mage (JDK 21) used for the rest of this project's Level 4 work, via a new JUnit test, org.mage.test.cards.interactions.cedh.DereviGaeasCradleTest#test_DereviCombatDamage_UntapsCradle_OneAttacker (not committed to this repo — see docs/RUN_CLASSIFICATION.md and rules_tests/gold_board_states/GBS-0010.json for the fixture record). Test setup: Derevi, Empyrial Tactician + Gaea's Cradle on the battlefield for playerA (no other permanents; playerB has none). Tapped Cradle for {G} in the precombat main phase (1 creature controlled = 1 green). Attacked with Derevi (unblocked, has flying). In the combat damage step, Derevi's trigger fired, targeting Gaea's Cradle with 'untap' chosen. After the trigger resolved, tapped the now-untapped Cradle again for a second {G} within the same combat damage step. Result: exactly 1 {G} in the mana pool at that checkpoint (the precombat {G} had already emptied per CR 500.5; this 1 {G} is entirely from the post-trigger retap), and Cradle remained on the battlefield. Passed 1/1 on the second attempt (first attempt failed with 'Missing CHOICE def' for the tap-or-untap effect's yes/no resolution choice, which needed to be registered as setChoice(playerA, true) after the target, not as a string choice before it). A follow-on two-attacker test to engine-verify the scaling claim did not complete successfully within this session's effort budget (failed with 'Can't find available command - manaActivate' on the second retap, suggesting the second trigger's untap did not take effect as sequenced) - not included in this record's verified evidence; see the scope note in prerequisites.other.

sources.reference: Independent reasoning about Derevi's combat-damage tap/untap trigger against Gaea's Cradle's mana ability, cross-checked against Commander Spellbook's variants index (query returned only the Emiel-dependent infinite version, confirming no infinite line exists with just these two cards).
